This March, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro and confirmed there are no plans for future Mac Pro hardware.

A new report published today by Bloomberg provides more background on Apple's Mac Pro strategy and reveals an unexpected detail about a product Apple once developed...

The inside story of Apple shelving the Mac Pro plans

In the latest issue of the Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman explains that "discontinuing the Mac Pro" was "not always the plan" internally at Apple. Gurman reiterated a point from earlier reporting: Apple's original idea was to release a so-called "Extreme" chip on top of the "Ultra" chip.

According to the report: "Apple is said to have developed both the M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme chips, but ultimately shelved these projects due to cost and demand considerations."

As for the specific Mac Pro hardware that was once in development, Gurman says Apple had two models in the works (codenamed J170 and J190), but they ultimately never made it to market.

Perhaps the most striking detail in the report is that one of them actually featured an Intel processor:

Apple finally discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removing it from its website and directing buyers to the Mac Studio instead. Although the ending was long foreshadowed, it still marks a sad end of an era for Mac Pro hardware enthusiasts.

What do you think about Apple's decision to abandon the Mac Pro product line rather than continue releasing "Extreme" chips in the Apple Silicon era? Let us know in the comments.
